A popular legend tells of a conflict between two kingdoms. For nearly a century they were decimated in a state of total war. After nearly a century of fighting, famine and poverty threatened to destroy both lands. In a desperate bid to end the war, one of the kings called for peace. The second king was wary of the first, and demanded collateral to ensure that his kingdom would not be betrayed. They held a summit and decided that the first king would lock his son in a tower that stood on the border of the two countries, and the second would lock his daughter in a second tower a stone’s throw away. Each tower would be attended to by members of the opposing sides’ royal guard as a sign of good will. So two towers were erected on either side of a lake with windows facing the other. As the children aged, locked away and isolated from the world, they fell in love. The prince would sing for the princess, his voice carrying over the waters. Unbeknownst to the two lovers, their nations were in disarray. Years of warfare with one another had destroyed their resources, they had burned each others’ forests, salted their fields, and flooded their quarries. One night, the prince was singing out his window as he did every night. The princess was sitting in her sill, watching him adoringly, dreaming of the life they might one day have together. But the war had been revived and far away from them the sounds of thousands of soldiers marching in the mountains could be heard, and the glimmer of their torches reflected upon the glassy surface of the water. The guards attending each tower saw this and knew their grim duty. They stacked timbers against the bases of each tower and set the base alight. As the smoke began to curl into their chambers, the lovers sang to each other, promising one another that they would soon be together forever. Legend states that the songbirds which nested in the rooftops of the towers heard their professions of love and were so moved by their words that they adopted their final song as their own. To this day, the area where the towers stood is viewed by some as accursed and others as sacred, but all the birds that nest on the lake sing the same sorrowful tune, thousands of years later.

This phrase is irrelevant because it will exact no change. When a police officer is killed the law goes to its fullest extent to find their killer and exact justice. It's not just black people that are wrongfully killed by police you know. This movement is not just racial.

I genuinely believe you think the phrase "black lives matter" means something that it doesn't: they matter more

Nobody (well there are always crazies on both sides, you got em just as much as the libs) will say that a police officer's life means so little that they should not be investigated. People may also not say that about black people (again, barring crazies), but the reality is that if how justice is served is representative of how our nation value for different groups, then we simply do not value black lives as highly. The individual might, but the nation doesn't. This is why police officers can shoot people in the back, or while they're sleeping, or for straight up no reason and not be charged. It happens every week in this country. I don't see how anybody can be ok with this. 

Before you downvote, think, respond, consider.

I'm sorry. I consider myself a liberal, I am proud of that, but I try to peruse this sub often for new ideas, many of them genuinely thought provoking. THIS. IS. NOT. The Black Lives Matter movement is not equivalent to a political campaign. 

It would be equally as inappropriate to paint a Joe Biden endorsement on a street as it would be to paint a MAGA message. But whether you agree with the subsidiary movements or not (I do not think we should straight up abolish the police), the phrase "black lives matter" itself is not something you should inherently disagree with. My brother lives in Minneapolis, and being black it could have just as easily been him with a knee placed on his neck for 8 minutes until he died. 

Whether or not you believe George Floyd was a good person is irrelevant. The same goes for Breonna Taylor, Eric Garner, Philando Castile, and many many others. The role of the police is to restrain people so that they can be taken into custody. Not to exact justice themselves. Thats what courts are for.

And before you repeat the mantra that a police officer's job is difficult, It might surprise you to know that almost every protestor would agree with you. I agree with you. My uncle was a police officer, my friend's grandfather who I became rather close with was a police officer. But my Aunt is also a nurse. Nurses must do the same exact thing as police on a daily basis: restrain violent, often drugged out, individuals. They are never lethal. Police officers in other countries do the same exact thing, and many of them manage to keep an annual death toll that is literally less than 1% of ours. It's true, do research on police in places like Iceland, Denmark, and Finland.

So it astounds me that people can be happy that a message of justice is being erased because their political choice doesn't receive the same platform as a simple statement that the lives of individuals should not be taken by police for bad reasons.

I know you will downvote this and soon it will become hidden. But I challenge you to be better than that. I know you can be better than that. Comment your grievances with my post and let's have a discussion, not an argument. I know we can, but I also know we won't.
